summary.text: A 59-year-old man was referred to outpatient physical therapy by his primary care physician for chronic peripheral vertigo of the right ear. He had dizziness and a spinning sensation lasting hours without identifiable triggers, with aural fullness, pressure, right ear ringing, nausea and vomiting. Symptoms began after COVID-19 2 years ago. His history included psoriasis, hypertension, seasonal allergies, tinnitus, hearing loss and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis; he is a retired Air Force pilot.

Brain MRI showed mild to moderate paranasal sinus disease and a small left mastoid effusion, and CT showed septal spurring, polypoid changes, ethmoid fullness, ostiomeatal obstruction and sinus mucosal thickening. He underwent bilateral nasal endoscopy with frontal sinusotomy, total ethmoidectomy and sphenoid and maxillary endoscopy, with a few weeks of relief before recurring symptoms and turbinate regrowth. Revision surgery was recommended; he started Dupixent, grew Staphylococcus aureus resistant to clindamycin, and used Bactroban and saline irrigation.

He sought a second opinion, where rigid nasal endoscopy showed mucosal edema, thin mucus stranding and inferior turbinate hypertrophy without polyps or purulence, and doxycycline was prescribed. He had historically responded to Cosentyx and doxycycline but not steroids, used Navage irrigation, and had weekly hyperbaric oxygen without benefit. Physical therapy examination found limited right cervical side bending, a positive right head impulse test and left-beating nystagmus, with right unilateral vestibular hypofunction possible.

Gaze stabilization and cervical stretching home exercises were prescribed, with physical therapy follow-up scheduled 4 weeks after the initial evaluation; travel limited his participation, and he had only two physical therapy visits. At the 4-week follow-up he had finished doxycycline and was taking Cosentyx and Dupixent. He denied dizziness or vertigo-like symptoms in weeks, a vestibular exam showed negative head impulse test and spontaneous nystagmus, and he reported complete resolution of dizziness after surgical and pharmacological treatment.
